text:
jamie: Heads-up 9 10 -- ran an onboarding import with the new adaptive-concurrency feature + paginator prefetch and ended up causing a client-side request jam that manifested as gateway 429s. Repro in staging.

jamie: Quick repro: sampleapp with `prefetch=3`, adaptive_concurrency_on=true, max_workers=12, importing ~200k tiny docs. After warmup the clients all expanded concurrency and we hit a long tail of 429s.

noor: Can you paste the relevant loop?

jamie: Sure:
```python
p = Paginator('/v1/embeds', page_size=100, prefetch=3)
adapter = AdaptiveConcurrency(min_workers=4, max_workers=64)
for page in p:
    adapter.scale_up_if_needed()
    batch = pack(page)
    submit_async(lambda: client.embed(batch))
```

diego: Looks like two problems combined: (1) adaptive scaler increases worker pool when latency spikes, but the scaler reacts to queue depth instead of server-side quota signals; (2) prefetch keeps filling the queue while gateway is telling us to throttle. Net: local autoscale amplifies server backpressure.

noor: Interesting. Our adaptive logic assumes server can absorb extra parallelism; that assumption breaks when quota is per-tenant token/sec or per-route cpu. We need to blend server feedback into scaling decisions.

jamie: In the run we saw logs: `2026-09-18T15:42:02Z gateway 429 quota_exceeded tenant=acct-test concurrent=48 path=/v1/embeds`. After 429s the client retried quickly (small base backoff) and the adaptive scaler bumped workers again -> second spike.

diego: Immediate mitigations we pushed to sampleapp: set default `adaptive_concurrency=false`, lower `prefetch` to 1, and add an `on_rate_limit` callback that temporarily disables autoscale for 5s. That dropped staging spikes to near-zero.

noor: Good quick fixes. Longer-term we should: (A) add a per-route "in-flight limiter" primitive in SDKs so the packer/adapter can't exceed N concurrent requests to a given route; (B) have adaptive scaler consume RateLimitEvents (Retry-After header or our RateLimitEvent) and enter a cooldown that decays slowly with successful responses; (C) change retry middleware to full jitter and larger base for POST 429s.

jamie: Agreed. Also worth adding a "cost_estimate" header to responses (infra work) so SDK can estimate tokens/compute per request and avoid sending oversized batches concurrently. Not necessary for initial fix but useful.

diego: For SDK parity: JS has an in-flight limiter already, but Py/Go/Rust/C# currently don't expose a reusable primitive. We should implement a small language-idiomatic limiter (semaphore + per-route counters) in each SDK and use it in AdaptiveBatcher and Paginator.

noor: Proposed API for limiter in SDK: `with client.route_limit('/v1/embeds', max_inflight=8): send()` and an `on_rate_limit` hook `client.on_rate_limit(route, consecutive, retry_after_ms)` so higher-level primitives can react.

jamie: I like that. Also add an optional `pause_prefetch_on_errors=true` to Paginator so it will stop fetching new pages after N consecutive 401/429 responses for that tenant/route. Default false for backwards compat.

diego: CI/QA asks: can we add deterministic tests that simulate a quota-limited proxy which returns 429 + Retry-After (float and date formats)? We want to assert the limiter prevents >N concurrent requests and that the scaler respects RateLimitEvents.

noor: Yes I'll add a staging harness and unit tests across SDKs. Plan: add test `BulkImport_Backpressure` to SDK CI that runs sampleapp against fake-proxy with a low concurrency budget and asserts no more than budget+1 concurrent server requests and no >2 spikes.

sdk-bot: created task: sdk/limiter-430 - implement per-route in-flight limiter in py/go/java/csharp/rust and add on_rate_limit hook.

infra-bot: noted: infra/headers-crypto - consider adding `X-Estimated-Server-Cost` header; created ticket infra/estimate-101.

jamie: Docs action: update onboarding quickstart to warn about mixing adaptive concurrency + prefetch and to recommend defaults (prefetch=1, adaptive=false, concurrency<=8) for first-run imports. Also add a short recipe for STS users (lock token refresh).

docs: On it. I'll add a "Bulk import best practices" section with examples, and a one-liner in the onboarding checklist.

diego: Implementation plan: 1) small hotfix to sampleapp defaults + add on_rate_limit callback (today); 2) implement limiter + on_rate_limit hook in Py & Go first and run staging ramps (this week); 3) extend to other SDKs and add CI tests (next sprint); 4) infra explore cost header (follow-up).

noor: One more nuance: adaptive scaler should decay conservatively after a cooldown; don't drop workers instantly because that causes thrashing. We'll add a ramp-down window of 30s with linear decay.

jamie: Great. Thanks team for quick triage. Marking follow-up to validate after Py/Go limiter PRs land and after two staging ramps. :white_check_mark:
